subject: Hybrid Ward Representation Recommendation
overview: The subcommittee reviewed research on demographics and election history to finalize a presentation regarding the composition of the Medford City Council. Members reached a consensus to recommend a hybrid ward representation system to improve diversity and voter engagement across the city.

items.title: Minutes
items.summary: Approved the minutes from the previous subcommittee meeting.

items.title: Presentation Planning
items.summary: Chair Ron Giovino outlined the strategy for a concise PowerPoint presentation to be delivered to the Committee of the Whole and the public.

items.title: Demographic Research Presentation
items.summary: Jean Zotter presented 2020 Census data highlighting Medford's increasing diversity and potential discrepancies in existing ward data.

items.title: Election Results and Voter Turnout
items.summary: Eunice Browne reviewed historic election results from 2001 to 2021, illustrating that most councilors have historically come from only two wards.

items.title: Voting Rights Case Study
items.summary: The subcommittee discussed the Lowell voting rights case and how ward-based systems are used to address issues of under-representation.

items.title: Surveys and Interviews Update
items.summary: Members reviewed feedback from over 360 survey respondents and several councilor interviews, noting a strong public preference for ward representation.

items.title: Pros and Cons of Ward Representation
items.summary: The committee debated potential drawbacks like increased politicization and decreased housing production versus the benefits of localized accountability.

items.title: Historical Governance Context
items.summary: Maury Carroll and Milva McDonald discussed Medford's 1986 transition from Plan E to a strong mayor government and previous failed attempts to establish ward seats.

items.title: Recommendation Straw Poll
items.summary: Conducted a straw poll indicating a majority of the subcommittee favors recommending a move to a hybrid ward representation system.

items.title: Public Participation
items.summary: A resident spoke in support of the move toward ward representation to improve localized governance.
